Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-16
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Novus - ML Infra Lead), Ethan Ross (Novus - Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (Novus - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): 28% throughput improvement after continuous batching config; need sustained 1-hr tests and production distribution to tune concurrency and queueing.

Topics: Benchmark numbers, batching/concurrency tuning, queueing and backpressure, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick check of attendees, we got maya, ethan, sofia and priya from our side. good?
[00:12] Maya Patel: yep, hi all, thanks. starting on time this week.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: hi, quick agenda: run through last week's perf numbers, look at continuous batching tweaks we applied, talk concurrency targets, then next steps.
[00:31] Ethan Ross: sounds good. we had the 10-min smoke tests yesterday that looked promising.
[00:36] Alex Chen: cool, priya you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:40] Priya Natarajan: yeah, i pushed the continuous batching change and bumped the max-batch-wait to 20ms for the p50-sensitive route. compared to baseline, throughput up about 28% for mixed small/medium requests. p50 latency is still within SLO 120ms, p95 crept from 280 to 340ms in bursts. so tradeoff is better overall throughput but some tail.
[01:05] Maya Patel: when you say mixed, what's the split? are we simulating production skew?
[01:10] Priya Natarajan: we used the sample distro you gave last week but scaled it to 200 qps. payload size breakdown was small (55%), medium (35%), large (10%). that's from the sample you exported, ethan, but it's synthetic.
[01:24] Ethan Ross: yes that's right, it roughly mirrors production but our real traffic has bigger spikes on morning sync. i'll share the full percentiles after this call.
[01:32] Sofia Martinez: quick sec, did you change any KMS or encryption when you enabled batching? security-wise?
[01:37] Priya Natarajan: no changes to KMS, it's purely serving runtime batching at the inference layer. data at rest and transit controls unchanged.
[01:44] Sofia Martinez: okay good, just wanted to confirm.
[01:47] Alex Chen: great. so the key findings: continuous batching at 20ms increases throughput 28% but p95 increases ~60ms. priya, do we have CPU/GPU utilization graphs?
[01:58] Priya Natarajan: yes, i pulled GPU util: baseline avg 62%, after change avg 78%, occasional 98% spikes during bursts. CPU host process had more variability due to serialization overhead. i attached the grafana snapshot in the slack thread.
[02:14] Maya Patel: interesting, so higher GPU utilization explains throughput lift. what was KV cache hit rate?
[02:19] Priya Natarajan: KV cache hit was stable at 12% for this workload, because many requests are new. caching will help more on repeated prefix patterns.
[02:27] Ethan Ross: what's the queueing behavior when we hit capacity? did you add a queue length cap?
[02:33] Priya Natarajan: yes, we set soft queue cap to 500ms and hard reject at 1200ms to avoid infinite queuing. with the new batching, we saw a small bump in average queue time (from 18ms to 38ms).
[02:45] Maya Patel: those numbers look reasonable; our SLO is p95 < 350ms end-to-end, so 340ms p95 is near the edge.
[02:54] Alex Chen: right, that suggests either reduce max-batch-wait or increase concurrency. we can also look at per-route concurrency targets. priya, what concurrency did we use?
[03:04] Priya Natarajan: the test used 8 concurrent streams per worker, with autoscaler set to scale at 70% GPU util, min instance 2, max 8.
[03:13] Ethan Ross: in our prod infra we tend to run with scale-to-zero off and min instances 4, but autoscaling reacts slower. would increasing min help?
[03:22] Priya Natarajan: yeah increasing min instances would reduce queuing on bursts but increases baseline cost. Another lever is to have a priority queue for latency-sensitive requests — small payloads get special routing with lower batch-wait.
[03:35] Maya Patel: can you do per-class routing? our request headers can include urgency flag.
[03:40] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood supports route-level config. we can pin a low-latency profile for p50-critical calls and a high-throughput profile for background. tradeoff is config complexity.
[03:50] Sofia Martinez: any implications for audit logs or tracing? we need to keep per-request audit for compliance.
[03:56] Priya Natarajan: no, audit logging is independent; we attach request IDs before batching so traceability stays intact. sometimes transcribers or autoscaling events can reorder logs but the request-id ties everything.
[04:09] Ethan Ross: good. ok, i want to understand the tail spikes — are they GC or queuing related?
[04:14] Priya Natarajan: early signs point to queue head-of-line blocking; when a large request lands in a batch it's slower. one mitigation is batch padding by size or priority-based batching to avoid mixing large with small in same batch.
[04:29] Maya Patel: how viable is padding? we worry about wasted compute with padding to max seq len.
[04:34] Priya Natarajan: you can cap pad to 75th percentile size for most requests, that reduces wasted work but helps latency. tradeoffs depend on model and quantization profile.
[04:45] Alex Chen: also quantization helps; if you run 4-bit quantization we saw lower per-token time but it can change kernel selection and that interacts with batching. any plans to test quantized model images?
[04:56] Maya Patel: yes we're evaluating q4 variants internally but haven't run them in POC yet. Ethan, can we schedule that?
[05:02] Ethan Ross: we can but need to confirm with infra about images. i'll add to the checklist.
[05:07] Alex Chen: ok next, priya did a short run simulating 100 concurrent clients for 10 minutes — results?
[05:14] Priya Natarajan: yes, 10-min stress at 100 conc showed stable throughput improvements, but we saw tail outliers around minute 6 and 9 — likely cluster scheduler/backpressure events. need longer sustained runs.
[05:26] Maya Patel: that's why we asked for 1-hour test earlier, to catch autoscaler and infra drift.
[05:31] Priya Natarajan: exactly. for the 1-hour run we'll capture kernel traces, GPU metrics, and the request distribution.
[05:38] Ethan Ross: what's the recommended concurrency target for production? we want predictable p95 < 350ms.
[05:44] Priya Natarajan: if you prioritize p95, aim for slightly lower concurrency per worker — 6 conc instead of 8 — and increase min instances. If you prioritize cost, use higher concurrency and batch-wait like 15-20ms.
[05:57] Maya Patel: cost vs latency — we need a sweet spot. our product teams value p95, but backend jobs can tolerate higher latency.
[06:05] Alex Chen: proposed approach: split traffic by route (latency-critical vs background), set low batch-wait (5-10ms) and lower concurrency for critical, and higher batch-wait for background. use autoscaler thresholds more aggressively to keep p95 headroom.
[06:20] Sofia Martinez: for compliance, any difference between Hosted vs Dedicated here? if we move to Dedicated we get predictable capacity but need to manage autoscaler and kernel updates locally?
[06:31] Priya Natarajan: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and you can pin kernel/quantization versions, plus network isolation. Redwood still provides control-plane features but you manage node-level updates if you want. audit logs and KMS integrate similarly.
[06:46] Maya Patel: cost question — do you have ballpark monthly for a min 4-instance Dedicated pool?
[06:52] Alex Chen: i'll send updated pricing after this call; depends on GPU type (A10G vs A100) and region. i'll include committed term discounts.
[07:01] Ethan Ross: ok. can we also get the perf runbook you mentioned? steps to reproduce, env vars, and checkpoints?
[07:07] Priya Natarajan: yes, i'll share a lightweight runbook with exact stress test command, sample distro file, and which traces to capture.
[07:14] Maya Patel: if priya shares the runbook and alex sends pricing, we can align internally and pick a date for the sustained run.
[07:21] Alex Chen: sounds good. any security blockers? sofia?
[07:24] Sofia Martinez: none right now — just need the audit log confirmation and the KMS unchanged note. we'll run our compliance checklist after the 1-hour run.
[07:33] Priya Natarajan: one more note: we saw kernel-level context switches in a small subset of runs; we'll include that in the logs. sometimes the infra scheduler preempts GPUs and that causes tail.
[07:44] Ethan Ross: that explains the minute-6 spike. we'll look at cluster scheduler logs.
[07:49] Alex Chen: ok quick recap and next steps, priya?
[07:54] Priya Natarajan: action items: run 1-hour sustained at 100 conc with attached distro and capture kernel traces; share grafana snapshots; produce runbook. i'll run the test and upload artifacts by Friday (2027-06-18).
[08:08] Ethan Ross: i'll send request distribution by Thursday (2027-06-17) and confirm min instances policy.
[08:15] Alex Chen: i'll send pricing and Dedicated options plus the perf runbook by Friday. we'll plan deep-dive 2027-06-23 unless that doesn't work.
[08:24] Maya Patel: that works for us. thanks everyone.
[08:28] Sofia Martinez: thanks all.
[44:30] Alex Chen: end of call — logging meeting notes and next steps in CRM. bye.

References: Slack thread with grafana snapshots (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), perf runbook (to be shared).
